```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os, sys, json, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, joblib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from scipy.stats import ks_2samp

def find_repo_root(start, name="CreditRiskLearning"):
    p_ = os.path.abspath(start)
    while True:
        if os.path.basename(p_) == name:
            return p_
        parent = os.path.dirname(p_)
        if parent == p_:
            raise FileNotFoundError(name)
        p_ = parent

REPO = find_repo_root(os.getcwd())
sys.path.append(os.path.join(REPO, "Core Resources"))
sys.path.append(os.path.join(REPO, "Core Resources", "Scripts"))
from python_style_util import p, f, s, C
from deck_utils import deck_style
deck_style()

PROJ = os.path.join(REPO, "Projects", "Flagship PD Model Project")
INPUT = os.path.join(PROJ, "02_PD_Model_Development", "inputs")
REG_CH = os.path.join(PROJ, "05_Applicant_PD_Dashboard", "registry", "lgbm_challenger_v1")
REG_CP = os.path.join(PROJ, "05_Applicant_PD_Dashboard", "registry", "logreg_baseline_v1")

# Challenger (refit) and champion, scored on the same test rows
lgbm = joblib.load(os.path.join(REG_CH, "model.joblib"))
with open(os.path.join(REG_CH, "metadata.json")) as fh:
    ch_meta = json.load(fh)
with open(os.path.join(REG_CH, "category_levels.json")) as fh:
    cat_levels = json.load(fh)
champ = joblib.load(os.path.join(REG_CP, "model.joblib"))
with open(os.path.join(REG_CP, "metadata.json")) as fh:
    cp_meta = json.load(fh)
FEATS = ch_meta["features"]
CAT = ch_meta["categorical"]

test_raw = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(INPUT, "test_raw.parquet"))
test_woe = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(INPUT, "test_woe.parquet"))
y_te = test_raw["TARGET"]

X_te = test_raw[FEATS].copy()
for col in CAT:
    X_te[col] = pd.Categorical(X_te[col], categories=cat_levels[col])

pd_ch = lgbm.predict_proba(X_te)[:, 1]
pd_cp = champ.predict_proba(test_woe[cp_meta["features"]])[:, 1]

gini_ch = 2 * roc_auc_score(y_te, pd_ch) - 1
gini_cp = 2 * roc_auc_score(y_te, pd_cp) - 1
uplift = gini_ch - gini_cp
ks_ch = ks_2samp(pd_ch[y_te.values == 1], pd_ch[y_te.values == 0]).statistic
BASE = y_te.mean()

# Rank ordering on test deciles, same method as 1.1c
rank = pd.Series(pd_ch).rank(method="first")
decile = pd.qcut(rank, 10, labels=False) + 1
dec = pd.DataFrame({"pd": pd_ch, "y": y_te.values, "decile": decile.values}).groupby("decile").agg(
    n=("y", "size"), rate=("y", "mean"), avg_pd=("pd", "mean"))

# Gain importance, share of total (from the saved refit)
imp = pd.Series(lgbm.booster_.feature_importance(importance_type="gain"), index=FEATS)
imp = (imp / imp.sum()).sort_values(ascending=False)

# Fit-row figures from notebook 03 section 4.2b (not recomputed here)
GAP_FIRST, GAP_REFIT = 0.065, 0.054
```

## The short version {.hero data-kick="Executive summary"}

::: {.hero-wrap}
::: {.hero-col}
<div class="hero-num">`{python} f"{uplift:+.3f}"`<small>Gini uplift over the scorecard</small></div>
:::

::: {.hero-col}
A gradient-boosted tree model on the **same 12 fields and the same applicants** finds only a modest gain over the scorecard:

- **Test Gini** `{python} f"{gini_ch:.3f}"` against the scorecard's `{python} f"{gini_cp:.3f}"`
- **Uplift** of `{python} f"{uplift:+.3f}"`, inside the "review" band, just below the "rebuild" line
- **Train/test gap** `{python} f"{GAP_REFIT:.3f}"` after one regularised refit, passing the 0.06 limit
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
**The scorecard stays champion.** The challenger finds a little more signal, but not enough to justify losing field-by-field explainability.
:::

## The question {data-kick="The question"}

The scorecard is easy to explain, but it only looks at each field's bins and how they add up. A tree model can find **interactions**: patterns where two fields matter more together than apart.

The test is fair. Both models score the same test applicants with the same 12 fields, so any difference is the model, not the data.

## Success criteria, set before fitting {data-kick="The bar"}

| Criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1.1a Gini uplift | Under 0.008: retain (noise). 0.008 to 0.03: retain and review interactions. Over 0.03: rebuild the scorecard. |
| 1.1b Train/test gap | At most 0.06 |
| 1.1c Rank ordering | Strictly rising across test deciles, zero reversals |
| 1.1d Calibration | Mean predicted risk within 0.44 pp of the actual rate |

## Did the first model overfit? {data-kick="The gap"}

The first LightGBM fit memorised its training rows. Its train/test gap was **`{python} f"{GAP_FIRST:.3f}"`**, above the 0.06 limit, so its uplift could not be used.

One refit with shallower trees and bigger leaves brought the gap to **`{python} f"{GAP_REFIT:.3f}"`** with no loss of test Gini. Only the refit is carried forward.

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| out-width: "90%"
labels = ["First fit", "Refit"]
gaps = [GAP_FIRST, GAP_REFIT]
colours = [p("gold", 300) if g > 0.06 else p("olive", 300) for g in gaps]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.2))
bars = ax.bar(labels, gaps, color=colours, width=0.45)
for b, v in zip(bars, gaps):
    ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width()/2, v + 0.002, f"{v:.3f}", ha="center",
            fontweight="bold", fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=12)
ax.axhline(0.06, color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
ax.text(1.3, 0.063, "1.1b limit 0.06", color="grey", fontsize=10, ha="right")
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.08)
ax.set_ylabel("Train minus test Gini")
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
```

## Test results: challenger against scorecard {data-kick="Results"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| out-width: "90%"
labels = ["Scorecard", "LightGBM refit"]
gini_vals = [gini_cp, gini_ch]
ks_vals = [ks_2samp(pd_cp[y_te.values == 1], pd_cp[y_te.values == 0]).statistic, ks_ch]
x = np.arange(2)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4))
w = 0.34
b1 = ax.bar(x - w/2, gini_vals, w, color=p("jacaranda", 300), label="Test Gini")
b2 = ax.bar(x + w/2, ks_vals, w, color=p("gold", 300), label="Test KS")
for bars in (b1, b2):
    for b in bars:
        ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width()/2, b.get_height() + 0.01, f"{b.get_height():.3f}",
                ha="center", fontsize=10, fontfamily=f("mono"))
ax.set_xticks(x, labels)
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.65)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
```

The refit's test Gini is `{python} f"{gini_ch:.3f}"`, an uplift of `{python} f"{uplift:+.3f}"`. That sits **0.0006 below the rebuild line**. The test Gini's standard error is about 0.008, so the honest reading is "retain, and treat as borderline."

## Rank ordering and calibration {data-kick="Checks"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| out-width: "90%"
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.2))
x = dec.index.values
ax.plot(x, dec["rate"].values * 100, marker="o", color=p("jacaranda", 300), linewidth=2.5, label="Actual default rate")
ax.plot(x, dec["avg_pd"].values * 100, marker="s", color=p("gold", 300), linewidth=2, linestyle="--", label="Predicted PD")
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xlabel("Risk decile (1 = lowest risk, 10 = highest)")
ax.set_ylabel("Default rate (%)")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
```

Risk rises with every decile, so the ranking passes (1.1c). The overall mean predicted risk is within a fraction of a percentage point of the actual rate, which passes 1.1d. Individual deciles differ by up to about 0.3 pp, with no consistent direction. That is a calibration detail to watch, not a failure.

## What the model relies on {data-kick="Drivers"}

Gain importance shows how much each field improves the trees. It is the tree equivalent of the scorecard's coefficients, but it doesn't show direction.

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Share of total gain, LightGBM refit"
imp_tbl = imp.to_frame("share of gain")
imp_tbl["share of gain"] = imp_tbl["share of gain"].map(lambda v: f"{v:.1%}")
imp_tbl
```

The external credit scores dominate, which matches the scorecard. The model is not telling a different story about which fields matter.

## Caveats {data-kick="Limits"}

- **Explainability.** A tree ensemble can't be read field by field the way the scorecard can. Explaining an individual decision needs an extra tool, such as SHAP, which hasn't been run yet.
- **Single model and seed.** One refit, one random seed. Seed sensitivity is not tested.
- **Target proxy.** Same payment-difficulty outcome as the scorecard, not a regulatory default.
- **Tuning.** No hyperparameter search. The refit was chosen by the train/test gap rule. The test Gini was shown before the refit, so the result is not a fully blind test.

## The call {data-kick="Recommendation"}

::: {.takeaway}
**Keep the scorecard as champion.** The LightGBM refit passes every check, but its uplift is small and borderline. The next step is to examine the tree's strongest interactions as candidate terms for a v2 scorecard, which keeps the explainability.
:::
